title: Scalar restriction comparison on specified condensed bar resolutions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent site of profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff and an inverse limit of finite discrete groups), with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Write $\mathcal M_A$ for internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and $\mathcal E_A$ for modules with $A$-linear $\underline G$-action and equivariant maps [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $U:\mathcal E_A\to\mathcal M_A$ forget the action and $\Gamma_G$ take the invariant submodule, fixed after every profinite base change. For a profinite parameter $S$, $A[S]$ is the free internal module on its representable condensed set; $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ is internal module Hom, right adjoint to tensor. Use the internal bar diagrams of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Let $\varphi:A\to A'$ be any morphism of commutative condensed rings, and let $\operatorname{Res}$ denote restriction of coefficients on internal modules and actions [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every profinite $S$, the free module $A[S]$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$, is flat (tensoring with it is exact), and $A[S][0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There are natural identifications
$$A'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A[S]\cong A'[S],\qquad
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[S],\operatorname{Res}M)\cong\operatorname{Res}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A'}(A'[S],M),$$
for internal $A'$-modules $M$, and a derived identification
$$R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[S],\operatorname{Res}M[0])\cong\operatorname{Res}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A'}(A'[S],M[0]).$$
Derived internal Hom is derived in the second variable in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The comparisons are normalized by the scalar-extension unit and restricted evaluation, natural in $S,M$, and for an equivariant $M$ commute with all inhomogeneous bar faces and degeneracies at $S=G^p$.
Let $a':N'[0]\to J^\bullet$ be a nonnegative equivariant $A'$-injective resolution and $a:(\operatorname{Res}N')[0]\to K^\bullet$ a nonnegative equivariant $A$-injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a complex $L$ over $B=A$ or $A'$, set $D_B(L)^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(B[\underline G^p],UL^q)$ and use its finite-diagonal total with differential $d_h+(-1)^pd_L$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. There exists an equivariant chain map $\beta:\operatorname{Res}J^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ with $\beta\operatorname{Res}a'=a$. Every such $\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism and, under the underived evaluation identifications above, induces quasi-isomorphisms on every column of
$$\operatorname{Res}D_{A'}(J)\cong D_A(\operatorname{Res}J)\xrightarrow{D_A(\beta)}D_A(K).$$
The canonical maps from the $\operatorname{Res}J$ columns to their derived internal Homs are isomorphisms after localization, equal to the restricted $A'$-resolution comparisons through the displayed derived scalar-Hom identification. The induced total map and invariant map $\operatorname{Res}\Gamma_G(J^\bullet)\to\Gamma_G(K^\bullet)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Their square with the invariant-to-total augmentations commutes term by term, both augmentation arrows are quasi-isomorphisms, and after localization its column identification is the evaluation-normalized derived scalar-Hom comparison above. The resulting square after inverting the augmentations is independent of $\beta$ and of the two resolutions. No flatness of $A'$ over $A$, or injectivity of $\operatorname{Res}J^q$ over $A$, is assumed.

proof.text: Transport to sheaves of section-ring modules using the underlying-sheaf-preserving equivalence and its exact tensor comparison. These identify internal Hom too: on section modules the right adjoint of $F\otimes-$ is the sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom(F,-)$ by the closed monoidal structure of module sheaves, and the tensor equivalence transports this right adjoint to internal module Hom. The free-linearization statement identifies $A[S]$ with the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$. This is precisely $j_{S!}A_S$, so the cited flatness theorem applies. The complex concentrated in degree zero is bounded above with flat terms and hence K-flat. The same assertions hold for $A'$. These categories have the required injective and K-injective resolutions by the action infrastructure, applied also to the trivial group.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text: The free adjunction and scalar adjunction identify $A'\otimes_A A[S]$ with $A'[S]$: the map sends $a'\otimes a[s]$ to $a'\varphi(a)[s]$, and its inverse sends $[s]$ to $1\otimes[s]$. The composites are the identity by the balanced relation and equality on generalized free generators. Since $A[S][0]$ is K-flat, ordinary scalar extension on this complex computes $A'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A[S]$. The scalar unit is $[s]\mapsto1\otimes[s]$. All formulas commute with maps of $S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text:
Put $P=A[S][0]$ and $P'=A'[S][0]$. The slice scalar-Hom chain adjunction, with first input $P$, gives a chain isomorphism
$$\theta_L:\operatorname{Res}\mathcal Hom_{A'}^\bullet(P',L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(P,\operatorname{Res}L).$$
It sends $f$ to $([s]\mapsto f([s]))$; its inverse extends $h([s])$ $A'$-linearly, $a'[s]\mapsto a'h([s])$. This proves the underived assertion at $L=M[0]$. The cited chain adjunction applies to arbitrary complexes and on every slice, so this is an identity of internal module sheaves, compatible with all profinite base changes, not just with pointwise global sections.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text:
Apply the derived scalar-Hom adjunction to $P$ and $QL$, using the free scalar-extension isomorphism of step 2. Invert its displayed isomorphism to obtain
$$\chi_L:R\mathcal Hom_A(P,\operatorname{Res}QL)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}R\mathcal Hom_{A'}(P',QL).$$
Here $Q$ is localization. Write $u_{B,L}$ for the canonical right-derived comparison $Q\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(B[S][0],L)\to R\mathcal Hom_B(B[S][0],QL)$. The precise normalization is
$$\chi_L\,u_{A,\operatorname{Res}L}\,Q\theta_L=\operatorname{Res}(u_{A',L}).\tag{*}$$
To check it, tensor by $P$ and transpose. Since $P$ is flat in degree zero, tensor by $P$ is exact and already computes its derived functor on every complex. The resolving-derived-adjunction normalization therefore identifies $u$ followed by derived evaluation with ordinary chain evaluation after localization. On either side of (*) the transpose sends $f\otimes[s]$ to $f([s])$, after the scalar unit $[s]\mapsto1\otimes[s]$ and restricted $A'$-evaluation. These are the same chain evaluation by step 3. The uniqueness of transposes and the evaluation characterization of the scalar-Hom comparison give (*). This proves the requested derived assertion at $L=M[0]$ and supplies its normalization on complexes without any injectivity assumption on $\operatorname{Res}L$.

proof.text: The identifications respect the entire bar diagram. Indeed evaluate on any generalized tuple $(g_1,\ldots,g_{p+1})$ after an arbitrary profinite base change. The first face on both sides sends $c$ to $g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{p+1})$, the interior faces replace $(g_i,g_{i+1})$ by $g_ig_{i+1}$, the last face drops $g_{p+1}$, and degeneracies insert $1$. The map $\theta$ does not change these evaluations or the action, so every face and degeneracy commutes. The scalar unit and restricted evaluation obey the same identities, so transposing as in step 4 gives the same compatibility for $\chi$. This includes parameter-dependent first faces because the calculation was on generalized sections on every slice.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text: For either coefficient ring, the categories of action modules and of modules are Grothendieck abelian; forgetting action is exact, and scalar restriction on both categories is exact, by the action infrastructure. Forgetting action also preserves injectives: apply exact split-coset induction with subgroup $1\subset G$. The quotient is $G$ and the section of $G\to G$ is the identity, so exact induction is left adjoint to forgetting action. The right-adjoint lemma then sends equivariant injectives to injective underlying modules. Invariants are left exact since they are right adjoint to exact trivial inflation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text: The resolution augmentation $a'$ is a monomorphism in every degree: in degree zero this is exactness of the injective resolution and in other degrees its source is zero. Exact scalar restriction makes $\operatorname{Res}a'$ a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. Apply the lifting theorem to $\alpha=\operatorname{Res}a'$, $\gamma=a$ and injective target $K^\bullet$. It supplies an equivariant chain map $\beta$ with $\beta\operatorname{Res}a'=a$ strictly. Any such $\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism: on cohomology its composite with the isomorphism $H^n(\operatorname{Res}a')$ is the isomorphism $H^n(a)$.

Fix $p$ and set $S=G^p$. By step 6, $UJ^q$ is injective over $A'$ and $UK^q$ is injective over $A$. The bounded-below complexes $UJ$ and $UK$ of injectives are therefore K-injective, so the units $u_{A',UJ}$ and $u_{A,UK}$ of the unbounded right derived functor are isomorphisms by its K-injective clause. Equation (*) makes $u_{A,\operatorname{Res}UJ}$ an isomorphism as well. Naturality of the derived unit gives
$$u_{A,UK}\,Q\mathcal Hom_A(P,U\beta)=R\mathcal Hom_A(P,QU\beta)\,u_{A,\operatorname{Res}UJ}.$$
Every factor on the right is invertible since $U\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence the column map is a quasi-isomorphism. Moreover $Q\beta\,Q\operatorname{Res}a'=Qa$ identifies both source and target with the same resolved module. The displayed naturality square and (*) show that its column identification is precisely the canonical comparison to derived Hom and the restricted $A'$-resolution comparison stipulated in the statement. This proves the stronger assertion about the actual comparisons, not only existence of column isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text:
Step 5 and equivariance of $\beta$ make
$$\operatorname{Res}D_{A'}(J)\cong D_A(\operatorname{Res}J)\longrightarrow D_A(K)$$
a map of first-quadrant double complexes with the stated signs. Each column is a quasi-isomorphism by step 8. The first-quadrant column-comparison theorem therefore makes its total a quasi-isomorphism. Scalar restriction identifies the source total with the total of the restricted diagram, because each total degree is the finite biproduct over $p+q=n$ and restriction is additive and exact. No infinite-product comparison is involved.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text: Apply the injective-bar-row theorem and then the bar-total-augmentation theorem to $J$ over $A'$ and to $K$ over $A$. Their hypotheses hold by step 6; the row theorem supplies exactly the required exact augmented horizontal rows. Hence $b_J$ and $b_K$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Restricted invariants equal invariants of the restricted action, since the fixed-section equations are unchanged. Likewise the restricted augmentation $\operatorname{Res}b_J$ is $b_{\operatorname{Res}J}$ under the identifications of steps 3 and 9. Exact scalar restriction makes this augmentation a quasi-isomorphism too; no application of the injective-row theorem to $\operatorname{Res}J^q$ is made.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text: The chain-map naturality clause of the bar-total-naturality theorem applies even to noninjective source complexes, so it applies to $\beta:\operatorname{Res}J\to K$. Its augmentation square commutes. Explicitly both paths take an invariant section $m\in J^q$ to the bar-zero element $\beta^q(m)\in D_A(K)^{0,q}$; all components with $p>0$ are zero. The two augmentations and the total comparison are quasi-isomorphisms by steps 9–10, so the same is true of $\operatorname{Res}\Gamma_G(J)\to\Gamma_G(K)$. Localize this actual square and invert its augmentation arrows. Its columns have exactly the evaluation-normalized identifications established in step 8.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent expansion of the scalar bar comparison.

proof.text:
For fixed resolutions, any two permitted $\beta$ agree on $\operatorname{Res}a'$. The uniqueness-of-lifts theorem, with bounded-below injective target $K$, makes them equivariantly homotopic. Applying invariants preserves this homotopy; applying the bar-total-naturality theorem gives the signed homotopy $(-1)^p\mathcal Hom_A(A[G^p],Uh)$ on totals. Thus both arrows of the augmentation square, and its localization with inverted augmentations, are independent of $\beta$.
For changes of resolutions choose augmentation-preserving chain lifts $j:J_1\to J_2$ and $k:K_1\to K_2$ by the same lifting theorem. The two maps $k\beta_1$ and $\beta_2\operatorname{Res}j$ to $K_2$ have identical composites with $\operatorname{Res}a'_1$, so the uniqueness-of-lifts theorem makes them homotopic. The preceding signed-homotopy formula and strict augmentation naturality identify the resulting squares. Lifts of the identity in reverse directions give inverse localized comparisons; uniqueness gives the identity and composition laws. The derived-unit normalization of step 8 is natural under these lifts, so these identifications also preserve the specified column comparisons.
